# LayerCal

> A free, browser-based calculator for deep learning models. Build a network by
> dragging layers onto a canvas and get parameter counts, forward-pass FLOPs and
> memory estimates in real time, then export the model as runnable PyTorch,
> TensorFlow or JAX code. Everything runs client-side: no account, no backend,
> nothing uploaded. Open source under the MIT licence.

LayerCal covers 14 layer types: Embedding, Linear, Conv2D, LSTM, GRU,
Transformer, Self-Attention, BatchNorm, LayerNorm, Dropout, MaxPool2D,
AvgPool2D, ReLU and Softmax.

An AI Architecture Advisor turns a plain-English description into a validated
layer stack. It is bring-your-own-key and supports Google Gemini, OpenAI and
Anthropic Claude. The user's API key stays in their browser and is sent only to
the provider they choose.

## Key formulas

- Embedding parameters: `vocab_size x embedding_dim`
- Linear parameters: `input_dim x output_dim + output_dim`
- Conv2D parameters: `in_channels x out_channels x kernel_size^2 + out_channels`
- LSTM parameters: `4 x (input_size x hidden_size + hidden_size^2 + 2 x hidden_size)` per layer, per direction
- GRU parameters: the LSTM formula with 3 gates instead of 4, so 75 percent of an LSTM
- Transformer block parameters: `12 x d_model^2 + 13 x d_model` when `d_ff = 4 x d_model`
- Self-attention parameters: `4 x (d_model^2 + d_model)`
- BatchNorm and LayerNorm parameters: `2 x num_features`
- Inference memory: `parameters x bytes_per_param`, where FP32 is 4 bytes, FP16 and BF16 are 2, INT8 is 1
- Adam training memory: `parameters x 16 bytes`, independent of weight precision, because the FP32 master copy the optimiser keeps cancels out the saving from mixed precision
- FLOPs: count a multiply-accumulate as 2 operations, so a Linear layer costs `2 x input_dim x output_dim`
